page: Microsoft Azure D48nlds_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an Intel processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. As part of the Dnldv6 family, the configuration is oriented around network-optimized and low-memory operational profiles while maintaining Premium Storage capability. It does not incorporate hardware accelerators or dedicated GPUs.

Integrated local storage is a primary architectural feature, delivering 2832 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD capacity. This local NVMe volume facilitates high-throughput scratch space and low-latency disk operations. In terms of external connectivity, the instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring routing through virtual networks or assigned IP resources. The 2.0 GB per core ratio represents an intentional hardware tradeoff, trading expansive memory capacity for core density and direct storage performance.

By omitting excess memory overhead and focusing on raw processor capacity alongside large local NVMe storage, the configuration achieves strong qualitative cost efficiency for compute-focused tasks. Microsoft Azure D48nlds_v6 is suited for batch processing, build and compilation pipelines, network appliance workloads, temporary ETL staging, and database workloads requiring rapid local caching.
